properties.name: Alloa Tower
properties.documentedDateText: 15th century, altered in the 16th, 17th and late 18th centuries
properties.shortDescription: A major late-medieval tower house and the principal surviving element of the Erskine family's Alloa estate.
properties.fullDescription: Historic Environment Scotland describes a 15th-century tower altered in the 16th, 17th and late 18th centuries. The tower is four storeys with an attic and is one of Alloa's most important surviving medieval structures.

properties.name: Kilncraigs
properties.shortDescription: The English Baroque office and factory building of Patons & Baldwins, reflecting Alloa's textile-industrial importance.
properties.fullDescription: A four-storey and attic office and factory building designed by William Kerr in 1903–04. It formed part of the Patons & Baldwins complex, whose Alloa roots extended back to the early 19th century.

properties.name: Northern Glass Cone, Alloa Glass Works
properties.statutoryStatus: Scheduled; listing removed because of dual designation
properties.shortDescription: The sole surviving glass cone in Scotland, associated with Alloa's glassmaking industry.
properties.fullDescription: Historic Environment Scotland dates the cone to around 1825. The Alloa glassworks was founded in 1750, and this approximately 79-foot structure survives from its 19th-century expansion.

properties.name: Thistle Brewery
properties.documentedDateText: Main brewery erected 1870–1871; earlier maltings and 17th/18th-century fabric survive
properties.shortDescription: A nationally important traditional brewery complex retaining early maltings, historic plant and an 1896 office.
properties.fullDescription: James MacLay began brewing in Alloa in 1830 and erected the Thistle Brewery in 1870–71. The complex includes early-19th-century maltings, earlier domestic fabric and historic brewing equipment.

properties.documentedDateText: Premises circa 1830; earlier oven; establishment dated 1810
properties.shortDescription: Historic commercial premises with an early-19th-century baking oven and a circa-1840 steam-powered oven.
properties.fullDescription: The street block is dated to around 1830 and incorporates earlier fabric. The rear brick oven may pre-date the shopfront, while the business fascia records the establishment of Hope Bakers in 1810.
